subject: Production latency surge — ZephyrAI / request for immediate regional redispatch
messages:
From: Miguel Santos <miguel@zephyr.ai>
To: soojin_lee@redwood.com
Cc: ops@zephyr.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:12:30 -0700
Subject: Production latency surge - inference p99 > 8s (us-west-2)

Hi Soojin,

We started seeing a sharp spike in inference p99 and error rate ~09:00 PDT on our prod endpoints routed to us-west-2. Symptoms:
- p99 latency jumped from ~650ms to >8s for text-generation route (model: rwd-13b-v1).
- Token throughput dropped ~45% and we saw a small but growing 5xx rate (0.7%).
- A subset of requests are timing out at the client side (3s timeouts) leading to many retries.

We attached a heap snapshot and a brief set of traces (heap_snapshot_0918.tar.gz). Our ops team checked the app layer and saw increased kernel-level interrupts on the inference nodes; we're not sure if it's a hardware or hypervisor noise issue.

Can Redwood flip routing for our account to another healthy AZ/region (us-west-1 or us-east-1) while you investigate? This is customer-impacting for our paying users and our on-call asked to escalate to execs if we don’t have a fast mitigation plan.

Thanks — Miguel
Miguel Santos
SRE Lead, ZephyrAI
From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel@zephyr.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:18:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency surge - inference p99 > 8s (us-west-2)

Acknowledged — thanks for the heads up, Miguel. Have escalated to ENG and platform on-call. Connor / team, can you triage the node telemetry and confirm if this is sectional (AZ) or account-wide?

Immediate ask: if ENG confirms an AZ-specific resource impedance, we should execute a controlled redispatch for ZephyrAI traffic to us-west-1 with an emergency TTL of 60s and enable prefix-level caching for their busiest routes. Miguel, please confirm you can accept a short-term cross-region failover (we'll coordinate CORS and edge locations).

I will also loop in Sales leadership for an exec comms/credit decision.

Sooj
Soojin Lee
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Miguel Santos <miguel@zephyr.ai>
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:34:44 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency surge - inference p99 > 8s (us-west-2)

Quick triage notes (preliminary):
- Scope: impact confined to us-west-2 backbone (most customer zones healthy). ZephyrAI traffic path shows queue starvation on a subset of pGPU hosts — sudden scheduler latencies correlate with host-level interrupts.
- 5xxs appear to be transient OOM/retry cascades, not model corruption.
- Candidate root causes: driver-level regression on the Nvidia stack or noisy neighbor kernel activities; hardware failure less likely but not ruled out.

Recommended immediate mitigation (Can do within ~8-12 minutes):
1) Redispatch 70% of ZephyrAI's traffic from us-west-2 -> us-west-1 (gradual ramp to avoid cold-cache shock).
2) Enable prefix/KV caching on ZephyrAI's top 8 routes for 30 minutes.
3) Increase instance pre-warm for their pool in us-west-1 to reduce cold starts.

I attached service traces (svc_traces_0918.log) and our interim playbook for a controlled redispatch (regional_redispatch_playbook_v1.pdf). If Soojin approves, I'll kick off the traffic steering now and post updates here.

—Connor
Principal SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: svc_traces_0918.log, regional_redispatch_playbook_v1.pdf
From: Miguel Santos <miguel@zephyr.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@zephyr.ai
Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:41:12 -0700
Subject: Re: Production latency surge - inference p99 > 8s (us-west-2)

Soojin / Connor — we authorize an emergency failover to us-west-1. Two asks before you proceed:
1) Rollback plan and expected customer-visible window (we want estimated duration and how to revert).
2) Confirmation on whether the failover will affect request semantics (latency, model versions, tokenization) — ZephyrAI runs model variants pinned to rwd-13b-v1-202608; any mismatches will break our validation.

If you can confirm (1) and (2), proceed. We are ready to accept the temporary regional shift — please loop in an exec if there will be credit or SLA discussions.

Miguel

- Customer: ZephyrAI (paid tier, monthly committed usage).
- Impact: elevated latency and small 5xx rate affecting production users; immediate mitigation recommended is cross-region redispatch to us-west-1 and prefix caching.
- Asks: approval for a one-time credit (proposed 20% of August invoice) and permission to proceed with the redispatch now.

If Jonas approves credit and the messaging, we'll coordinate a short customer note (we should be explicit on timing and revert conditions).

Hannah Schmitt

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 18 Sep 2026 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Approval: proceed with redispatch and one-time credit

Approved. Thanks for the clear remediation plan and Connor for the quick triage. Decisions:
- Immediate action: Proceed with the planned gradual redispatch (70% -> us-west-1 over 10 minutes) and enable the prefix/KV caching for the specified routes. Connor, proceed now and post status updates every 10 minutes.
- Customer relief: Approve a one-time credit equal to 20% of the August invoice, to be applied immediately after we confirm service stabilization. Hannah, please prepare the customer-facing note; keep it factual: cause under investigation, mitigation executed, rollback criteria, and credit commitment.
- Escalation: If errors or latency do not improve within 45 minutes, we will escalate to an executive bridge and consider expanding to us-east-1 for broader load relief.

I am available for the exec bridge if needed. Please confirm when the redispatch is complete and share the trimmed incident report (include attached traces).

Jonas Weber
VP, Customer Success & Partnerships
Redwood Inference
